column11: Graviton gives better price/performance if app supports ARM
Dev workload — ideal for ARM cost savings

column1:
t3a was selected because it delivers immediate cost savings while remaining on the same x86 architecture as the current environment, which means no application rebuilds, no dependency compatibility risks, and no CI/CD or container pipeline changes. It was the safest way to meet the RFP performance requirements while minimizing operational and migration risk, especially for production workloads. t4g (Graviton) offers better price-performance, but it introduces an architecture shift to ARM, which requires validation of containers, libraries, antivirus engines, and monitoring agents. Because of this, t4g is a strong option but is still relatively newer in many enterprise stacks.

A safer approach would be to adopt t4g first in DEV and UAT, keeping PROD on the more mature and fully compatible x86-based t3a family. Using this mixed-family approach, the estimated cost for 1-year reserved instances is ≈ $367/month. Once t4g is validated and stable in DEV and UAT, we can plan to shift PROD to t4g, which could reduce the total monthly cost to ≈ $301/month.
